steps.decision: Baseline seal strength approximately symmetric and consistent with normality (AD p=0.24, Shapiro p=0.485).
Shapiro-Wilk fails to reject normality (p=0.485); baseline data treated as normal for capability analysis.
No individual points out of control limits; 2 moving-range points exceeded the MR-UCL, indicating occasional excess point-to-point jumps but overall process appears stable/in control on individuals.
Mean seal strength (52.35N) is statistically significantly below the 55N margin requirement.
Mean seal strength is statistically significantly above the 45N minimum (LSL), i.e. the minimum spec is comfortably met on average.
One-sided capability against LSL=45N only (no USL exists): Cpk~0.67 (short-term, MR-based sigma), Ppk~0.64 (long-term, overall sigma). Both well below the conventional 1.33 capability threshold.
75% (45 of 60) of baseline seals fall below the 55N required margin; only 1.7% (1 of 60) fall below the 45N minimum spec.

Full factorial model (bead_spacing, bond_angle, cure_temperature, all interactions) is not significant overall (p=0.834); no individual main effect or interaction reached p<0.05 (smallest term p=0.287, the 3-way interaction). None of the three screened assembly settings account for seal-strength variation in this run.

Declared any_factor_significant=false based on step 8. This does not satisfy the gate (any_factor_significant==true) required to release the composite/RSM design batch and the confirmation-run batch; steward returned refusal=locked for both. No further DOE optimization data exists to pull honestly.
